title: AirLLM enables local 70B AI #airllm #flashattention #llama3
description:
AirLLM makes it possible to run a 70B-parameter AI model without a supercomputer. The open-source Python library streams model layers from a hard drive instead of loading the entire model into memory at once.

That layer-by-layer approach, combined with FlashAttention, keeps memory usage nearly flat even for long prompts. As a result, models like LLaMA 3.3 70B can run on a MacBook or gaming PC rather than requiring expensive high-end infrastructure.

For students, researchers, and indie developers, this lowers the hardware barrier to advanced local AI. The broader shift is clear: large-model inference is becoming more accessible, cheaper, and practical on consumer machines.

top_comments.text: You conveniently "forget" to mention that this is a tradeoff of memory and speed. You can run big models, but so slow that you will probably get frustrated.

top_comments.author: @miketheleisureman2334
top_comments.text: Where it could make sense : offline jobs where nobody waits. Run it overnight on a stack of documents. Useless where someone is watching a screen, which is every client-facing thing you would build.

top_comments.author: @miketheleisureman2334
top_comments.text: A 70B model needs roughly 140GB of memory to run normally, which means data-center GPUs. Tools like AirLLM get around that by never holding the whole model at once. They load one slice, compute, drop it, load the next. So your small machine only ever holds a fraction.

top_reply.author: @JulienGordon
top_reply.text: It doesn’t need 140gb. Memory size depends on quantization. Total size depends on context window. Can be run very very well on 128GB  Mac Pro. We need to stop this madness. Rampant consumerism and “More is better” mentality helps only the folks that make the hardware while delivering marginal benefits to all. Most ppl don’t need a 70B parameter model to help them do whatever. 9B that’ll run on most hardware will do a great job at 99% of office type tasks.

top_comments.author: @hypercho
top_comments.text: AirLLM's slice-based approach is genuinely clever — loading model chunks on demand instead of holding the full 70B in memory. For privacy-first local AI builds where the machine is yours alone, the speed tradeoff is worth it. This is the kind of optimization that makes running large models on consumer hardware actually viable.
